evidence.claim: The Claude Code 2.1.88 package snapshot tells the model to respond to permission denial by adjusting its approach, prefer dedicated tools over Bash when available, parallelize independent tool calls, and keep user-facing output concise.

WWriting's current buildSystemPrompt combines identity, a JSON-fence tool protocol, start_run and queue_chapters workflow rules, rendered tool documentation, output style, and a changing project snapshot in one system message, even though native tools are also sent to compatible providers.

WWriting's provider adapter contains a separate WRITING_TOOL_DEFINITIONS table and injects a chapter-writer system identity based on the allowed tool count, creating a second prompt and tool-description path outside the chat registry.

The ready implementation plan adds typed tool schemas, autonomous /init modelInstruction expansion, arbitrary Shell, risk classification, task grants, unified chat_activity events, and confirmation flows, but scopes these changes primarily through the chat-agent path rather than a single shared Agent runtime.
WWriting already distinguishes stable and dynamic chapter prompt blocks and has repository research documenting that changing dynamic content inside the stable prefix harms cache reuse.
WWriting describes itself as a local desktop long-form novel Agent whose chapters and durable project artifacts remain in the user's project folder and can be inspected with ordinary file tools.

recommendations.statement: Build one PromptAssembler and one byte-stable Static Core shared by chat and chapter workflows; remove duplicate natural-language tool catalogs and provider-layer role prompts.
recommendations.acceptance_signal: Static Core contains no project snapshot, permission value, tool list, or task content; chat and chapter requests produce the same Static Core hash.

recommendations.statement: Represent Runtime Policy, Project Instructions, Workflow Policy, and Dynamic Context as named ordered layers owned by the unified Agent runtime.
recommendations.acceptance_signal: Snapshot tests attribute every prompt segment to one layer, and changing progress, permissions, or workflow changes only the expected layer.

recommendations.statement: Validate prompt behavior through a provider matrix covering generic file work, deep-tool chapter submission, permission denial, stop and resume, /init, and prompt-injection isolation.
recommendations.acceptance_signal: At least two OpenAI-compatible models complete every scenario using native schemas without a duplicated textual tool directory, and every completion claim traces to a tool result or runtime terminal state.
